title: Technical Companion: A Functional Model of Jeevan

passages.text: Scope: This companion formalises the interpretation developed in Jeevan Architecture. It represents the five faculties, their paired activities, acquired organisation, embodied expression, evaluation, and continuity in a precise qualitative notation. The primary texts do not state this formalism. Their direct claims, the cross-text synthesis built from them, and the remaining textual variants are kept distinct below.

The formalism is optional. It can be rejected without changing the primary-text account in the reader note or the documentary assignment of the sixty-one pairs in The Sixty-One Activity Pairs of Jeevan.
Dotted underline: definition · Blue underline: link

passages.heading: 1-commitments-and-boundaries
passages.text: 1. Commitments and boundaries

passages.heading: 1-commitments-and-boundaries
passages.text: Four levels of claim must not be merged.

passages.heading: 1-commitments-and-boundaries
passages.text: Primary-text claims. Jeevan is one constitutionally complete sentient atom with five faculties and ten paired activities. The activities are found in state and motion, and the detailed enumeration contains 122 activities in sixty-one pairs. Delusion, awakening, the four-and-a-half effective activities, the four values, bodily mediation, and continuity across bodily death are also stated in the primary texts.

passages.heading: 1-commitments-and-boundaries
passages.text: Cross-text synthesis. The five faculties can be presented as an ordered activity architecture in which an inwardly established orientation becomes effective through the adjoining outward faculties and the body. Sanskar can be read as acquired organisation spanning buddhi, chitta, vritti, and mun, held in relation to realisation at atma.

passages.heading: 1-commitments-and-boundaries
passages.text: Formal commitments. Product state spaces, time indices, partial functions, reception predicates, ordered compositions, an inquiry protocol, qualitative success conditions, and a carriage relation across embodiments belong to this model alone.

passages.heading: 1-commitments-and-boundaries
passages.text: Unsettled matters. The relation between state–motion and projection–reflection, the operation of the jeevan–body connection, the exact scope of sanskar, and the provenance of an orally reported twelvefold practical schema remain open.

passages.heading: 1-commitments-and-boundaries
passages.text: The model concerns jeevan, not satta. Omnipresence is actionless Knowledge and the reality with which understanding is to agree. The sources nevertheless call it the basis and source of inspiration for activity, with inspiration inherent through saturation (MVD, pp. 35–36, 174). The formalism represents that standing availability as a reference rather than inventing an acting source of instructions. The body is also outside the modelled state of jeevan. It is the temporary embodied medium through which selection becomes conduct and bodily, material, and relational consequences become available for evaluation (MVD, pp. 199–205).

passages.heading: 1-commitments-and-boundaries
passages.text: The intrinsic activity of jeevan and the conditional embodied branch

passages.heading: 2-faculty-wise-state-and-activity
passages.text: 2. Faculty-wise state and activity

passages.heading: 2-faculty-wise-state-and-activity
passages.text: Let the ordered set of faculties be

passages.heading: 2-faculty-wise-state-and-activity
passages.text: F={a,b,c,v,m}:={atma,buddhi,chitta,vritti,mun}.

passages.heading: 2-faculty-wise-state-and-activity
passages.text: Let Fout={b,c,v,m} and define the adjoining inward faculty by

passages.heading: 2-faculty-wise-state-and-activity
passages.text: in⁡(b)=a,in⁡(c)=b,in⁡(v)=c,in⁡(m)=v.

passages.heading: 2-faculty-wise-state-and-activity
passages.text: Each faculty f∈F is assigned a qualitative state space X(f). The state of jeevan is represented analytically as

passages.heading: 2-faculty-wise-state-and-activity
passages.text: X(J,t)=(x(a,t),x(b,t),x(c,t),x(v,t),x(m,t)).

passages.heading: 2-faculty-wise-state-and-activity
passages.text: The product notation does not divide jeevan into five agents or spatial stores. It records the distinct activity attributed to each faculty within one indivisible unit.

passages.heading: 2-faculty-wise-state-and-activity
passages.text: 2.1 Acquired and presently active organisation

passages.heading: 2-faculty-wise-state-and-activity
passages.text: The sources locate the attained awakening called sanskar in mun, vritti, chitta, and buddhi while placing realisation at atma (MVD, pp. 121, 315, 323). The model therefore lets

passages.heading: 2-faculty-wise-state-and-activity
passages.text: Facq={b,c,v,m}

passages.heading: 2-faculty-wise-state-and-activity
passages.text: and represents each outer coordinate as an enduring acquired aspect s(f,t) together with a presently active aspect q(f,t):

passages.heading: 2-faculty-wise-state-and-activity
passages.text: x(f,t)=(s(f,t),q(f,t))(f∈Facq),x(a,t)=q(a,t).

passages.heading: 2-faculty-wise-state-and-activity
passages.text: Thus

passages.heading: 2-faculty-wise-state-and-activity
passages.text: S(J,t)=(s(b,t),s(c,t),s(v,t),s(m,t)),Q(J,t)=(q(a,t),q(b,t),q(c,t),q(v,t),q(m,t)).

passages.heading: 2-faculty-wise-state-and-activity
passages.text: S and Q are analytical aspects, not two stores. Restricting acquired organisation to four faculties is a reading of the passages, not an explicit storage theory. A formulation in which awakening of the four implicitly includes a transformed relation to atma remains compatible with the sources.

passages.heading: 2-faculty-wise-state-and-activity
passages.text: 2.2 The paired activities

passages.heading: 2-faculty-wise-state-and-activity
passages.text: Let Bf denote the activity classified as bal in the tabulated activity-level enumeration:

passages.heading: 2-faculty-wise-state-and-activity
passages.text: Ba=anubhav,Bb=bodh,Bc=chintan,Bv=tulan,Bm=asvadan.

passages.heading: 2-faculty-wise-state-and-activity
passages.text: Let Pf denote its paired shakti activity:

passages.heading: 2-faculty-wise-state-and-activity
passages.text: Pa=pramanikta,Pb=sankalp,Pc=chitran,Pv=vishleshan,Pm=chayan.

passages.heading: 2-faculty-wise-state-and-activity
passages.text: The activity-level assignment is directly tabulated in AVD, pp. 91–94, and the ordering agrees with every paired heading in MVD, pp. 328–348. Interpreting Bf as an established qualitative state and Pf as its outward efficacy is the model’s functional reading. These symbols name activities; they are not functions.

passages.heading: 2-faculty-wise-state-and-activity
passages.text: The realisation-based dependency order is represented as

passages.heading: 2-faculty-wise-state-and-activity
passages.text: Bout=⟨Ba,Bb,Bc,Bv,Bm⟩,

passages.heading: 2-faculty-wise-state-and-activity
passages.text: corresponding to

passages.heading: 2-faculty-wise-state-and-activity
passages.text: anubhav→bodh→chintan→tulan→asvadan.

passages.heading: 2-faculty-wise-state-and-activity
passages.text: The paired activities that make this organisation effective outward are ordered as

passages.heading: 2-faculty-wise-state-and-activity
passages.text: Pout=⟨Pa,Pb,Pc,Pv,Pm⟩.

passages.heading: 2-faculty-wise-state-and-activity
passages.text: The angle brackets record order and dependence, not composition or conversion. Realisation does not turn into enlightenment as one substance becoming another; each faculty performs its own activity in relation to the orientation available from the faculty inward of it.

passages.heading: 2-faculty-wise-state-and-activity
passages.text: The independence of these ordered paths from the direction terms paravartan and pratyavartan is a hypothesis. AVD places the bal activities under pratyavartan and the shakti activities under paravartan, while MVD, pp. 276–277, orders the state activities outward in the realisation-based way. The model keeps the tension explicit rather than treating either arrangement as a settled identity.

passages.heading: 2-faculty-wise-state-and-activity
passages.text: 2.3 Symbols used below

passages.heading: 2-faculty-wise-state-and-activity
passages.text: Let T be the set of time indices within an embodied life. For f∈F, C(f) denotes contents or orientations available at f, γf(t)∈C(f) the manifest orientation at time t, and I(f) inquiries borne at f. Let SJ and QJ be the respective ranges of S(J,t) and Q(J,t), and Qpass the possible results of a completed inquiry pass. Y denotes observable embodied consequences, Pbody possibilities selected for bodily expression, Bgross bodily states, Efield surrounding conditions, and Γ the relevant context of relationship, bodily condition, means, and circumstance.

passages.heading: 2-faculty-wise-state-and-activity
passages.text: §§2–8 suppress the embodied-life index; §9 restores it. Thus X(J,n,t), S(J,n,t), and Q(J,n,t) are the same quantities for life n at time t, not functions of a different arity.

passages.heading: 3-receptivity-and-reflective-accord
passages.text: 3. Receptivity and reflective accord

passages.heading: 3-receptivity-and-reflective-accord
passages.text: An outer faculty does not become consonant with the one inward of it merely because an indication is available. The four reception conditions and their social or educative supports are set out in the reader note §3.2 (MVD, pp. 282–286).

passages.heading: 3-receptivity-and-reflective-accord
passages.text: For f∈Fout, define

passages.heading: 3-receptivity-and-reflective-accord
passages.text: r:Fout×T⟶{⊤,⊥}.

passages.heading: 3-receptivity-and-reflective-accord
passages.text: r(f,t)=⊤ means that the stated absence-condition at f is sufficiently met for f to receive the orientation of in⁡(f) at t. This is a binary modelling simplification. The passages describe success and failure, while receptivity elsewhere admits of extent; a graded account may ultimately be required (MVD, pp. 142, 248, 284).

passages.heading: 3-receptivity-and-reflective-accord
passages.text: This predicate is not identified with an inward use of the pair-member Pf. The primary text states that internal regulation of jeevan’s powers produces the ability to receive; it does not state that resolve, visualisation, analysis, or selection is itself reversed or supplied with a direction parameter.

passages.heading: 3-receptivity-and-reflective-accord
passages.text: For each outer faculty, let Accord⁡f⊆C(f)×C(in⁡(f)) be the model’s qualitative relation “according to the adjoining inward orientation.” Reflective accord is represented by

passages.heading: 3-receptivity-and-reflective-accord
passages.text: Π(f,t)=⊤ ⟺ r(f,t)=⊤ ∧ Accord⁡f(γf(t),γin⁡(f)(t)).

passages.heading: 3-receptivity-and-reflective-accord
passages.text: Full directional pratyavartan is the conjunction of this accord across the four adjoining faculty relations. This formalises the directional sense adopted in the reader note; it does not exclude the recognising-and-fulfilling and understanding-and-teaching uses found elsewhere in the corpus (SB, pp. 63–64; KD §3.12, p. 110).

passages.heading: 3-receptivity-and-reflective-accord
passages.text: Three of the four conditions depend on social or educative arrangements. The effective activity of an individual jeevan is therefore not modelled as self-sufficient: orderliness, relationship, study, and an evidence-bearing tradition form part of the conditions under which deeper understanding becomes effective.

passages.heading: 4-embodied-consequence-inquiry-and-change
passages.text: 4. Embodied consequence, inquiry, and change

passages.heading: 4-embodied-consequence-inquiry-and-change
passages.text: Let B(t)∈Bgross denote the present body and E(t)∈Efield the surrounding relationships, work, society, material conditions, and nature. A selected possibility p(t) is made available for embodied expression:

passages.heading: 4-embodied-consequence-inquiry-and-change
passages.text: Express:X(J)×Γ⇀Pbody,

passages.heading: 4-embodied-consequence-inquiry-and-change
passages.text: p(t)=Express(X(J,t),χ(t)),χ(t)∈Γ,

passages.heading: 4-embodied-consequence-inquiry-and-change
passages.text: when an orientation becomes selected for bodily expression. Express represents the ordered contribution of resolve, visualisation, analysis, and selection without treating their activity labels as composable functions. Embodied change and its observable consequence are represented by

passages.heading: 4-embodied-consequence-inquiry-and-change
passages.text: G:Bgross×Efield×Pbody⟶Bgross×Efield,H:Bgross×Efield⟶Y,

passages.heading: 4-embodied-consequence-inquiry-and-change
passages.text: G includes speech, bodily execution, work, interaction, and material change. H makes bodily condition, performed action, material result, and another person’s response available for evaluation. The source passages name bodily waves, prana, heart, medhas, cognitive and work organs, behaviour, and gratification, but do not supply one serial mechanism joining them (MVD, pp. 199–205).

passages.heading: 4-embodied-consequence-inquiry-and-change
passages.text: 4.1 A proposed inquiry protocol

passages.heading: 4-embodied-consequence-inquiry-and-change
passages.text: The sources place curiosity in mun, describe samvahan as bearing inquiry, and connect study with the learner’s need and questions (MVD, pp. 77–78, 248, 313–314, 344). They also give a developmental sequence from curiosity in mun through enthusiasm in vritti, delight in chitta, elation and immersion in buddhi, and realisation in atma (MVD, pp. 77–78). That sequence concerns the inward regulation of energies toward awakening; it is not the consequence-to-question protocol below. The texts do not give this protocol, which is introduced only to distinguish consequence, question, understanding, and reflective accord.

passages.heading: 4-embodied-consequence-inquiry-and-change
passages.text: An embodied consequence may occasion an inquiry:

passages.heading: 4-embodied-consequence-inquiry-and-change
passages.text: Occ:Y×X(J)⇀I(m).

passages.heading: 4-embodied-consequence-inquiry-and-change
passages.text: When Occ is undefined, no question follows from that consequence. When it is defined, an inquiry may be borne toward an inward faculty:

passages.heading: 4-embodied-consequence-inquiry-and-change
passages.text: Bear(f):I(f)⟶I(in⁡(f)).

passages.heading: 4-embodied-consequence-inquiry-and-change
passages.text: An inward faculty may make an answer available from its current organisation,

passages.heading: 4-embodied-consequence-inquiry-and-change
passages.text: Answer(f):X(in⁡(f))×I(in⁡(f))⇀C(f),

passages.heading: 4-embodied-consequence-inquiry-and-change
passages.text: and the outer faculty may take that content up:

passages.heading: 4-embodied-consequence-inquiry-and-change
passages.text: Uptake(f):X(f)×C(f)×T⇀X(f).

passages.heading: 4-embodied-consequence-inquiry-and-change
passages.text: The uptake map is defined only where reception is available:

passages.heading: 4-embodied-consequence-inquiry-and-change
passages.text: Uptake(f)(x,γ,t)↓⟹r(f,t)=⊤.

passages.heading: 4-embodied-consequence-inquiry-and-change
passages.text: Reception and change are separate. A question may remain unanswered; an answer may be heard without changing the outer faculty; a passing thought need not become enduring sanskar. When bearing, answering, and uptake are all defined, their result is denoted Q(t)∈Qpass. If uptake makes γf(t) accord with the adjoining inward orientation, then Π(f,t)=⊤; neither Q(t) nor a bodily consequence is itself the definition of pratyavartan.

passages.heading: 4-embodied-consequence-inquiry-and-change
passages.text: Let the two analytical update maps be

passages.heading: 4-embodied-consequence-inquiry-and-change
passages.text: UQ:QJ×Qpass×SJ⟶QJ,US:SJ×Qpass⇀SJ.

passages.heading: 4-embodied-consequence-inquiry-and-change
passages.text: Present activity and enduring organisation may then be represented as

passages.heading: 4-embodied-consequence-inquiry-and-change
passages.text: S(J,t+1)=US(S(J,t),Q(t))when uptake occurs and the content is assimilated.

passages.heading: 4-embodied-consequence-inquiry-and-change
passages.text: The stronger printed learning sequence should govern interpretation of these symbols: realisation-oriented conceptions in buddhi become thought and action, and thoughts arising through action are instilled again as sanskar through inference (MVD, p. 218). The formal protocol must not replace that source-grounded account.

passages.heading: 5-correctness-incompleteness-and-evidence
passages.text: 5. Correctness, incompleteness, and evidence

passages.heading: 5-correctness-incompleteness-and-evidence
passages.text: The model treats bodh and anubhav as success terms rather than fallible estimates. Let K denote reality as the Knowledge-reference, and let Agree⁡(x,K) be the model’s qualitative agreement relation between a candidate content x and that reference:

passages.heading: 5-correctness-incompleteness-and-evidence
passages.text: Bodh:X(c)⇀X(b),Bodh(xc)↓⟹Agree⁡(xc,K)=⊤,xc∈X(c),

passages.heading: 5-correctness-incompleteness-and-evidence
passages.text: Anubhav:X(b)⇀X(a),Anubhav(xb)↓⟹Agree⁡(xb,K)=⊤,xb∈X(b).

passages.heading: 5-correctness-incompleteness-and-evidence
passages.text: If agreement is absent, the candidate remains assumption, judgment, or unresolved meaning rather than becoming incorrect bodh or anubhav. This is a formal interpretation of the success vocabulary, not a source formula. The condition of a perturbed or unenlightened buddhi is represented by the functions being undefined for the content, not by a false result.

passages.heading: 5-correctness-incompleteness-and-evidence
passages.text: Incompleteness may concern subject matter, coordination, or evidence. Let D be the domain of subject matters considered by the model, and let Δ(b) and Δ(a) be the subdomains for which enlightenment and realisation are effective:

passages.heading: 5-correctness-incompleteness-and-evidence
passages.text: Δ(a)⊆Δ(b)⊆D.

passages.heading: 5-correctness-incompleteness-and-evidence
passages.text: The inclusions and the domain model are analytical. They allow incomplete reach without introducing partly false realisation.

passages.heading: 5-correctness-incompleteness-and-evidence
passages.text: Knowledge is not complete in the model merely because an inner state is coherent. It must become intelligible, directive in activity, embodied competently, evaluated in relationship, and conveyable to another. This requirement follows the primary evidence chain from realisation through behaviour, experiment, and awakened tradition (MVD, p. 12; JV, p. 26).

passages.heading: 6-values-and-two-qualitative-judgments
passages.text: 6. Values and two qualitative judgments

passages.heading: 6-values-and-two-qualitative-judgments
passages.text: Let A(f,t) hold when immersion is present at f∈{b,c,v,m}:

passages.heading: 6-values-and-two-qualitative-judgments
passages.text: When A(f,t)=⊤, the value is named by the faculty:

passages.heading: 6-values-and-two-qualitative-judgments
passages.text: Value⁡(b)=bliss,Value⁡(c)=contentment,Value⁡(v)=peace,Value⁡(m)=happiness.

passages.heading: 6-values-and-two-qualitative-judgments
passages.text: Let H(f,in⁡(f),t) denote qualitative concurrence between adjoining faculties. It is a relation assessed at a time, not the embodied-consequence map H of §4. The correspondence between immersion and adjoining concurrence is represented as

passages.heading: 6-values-and-two-qualitative-judgments
passages.text: The sources give both formulations and their term-for-term correspondence; the biconditional is the model’s logical sharpening (MVD, pp. 307, 327).

passages.heading: 6-values-and-two-qualitative-judgments
passages.text: Discord is represented by the failure of one or more such relations. The thirst for restfulness is present when at least one remains unresolved:

passages.heading: 6-values-and-two-qualitative-judgments
passages.text: Trisha⁡(t)=⊤ ⟺ ∃f∈{b,c,v,m}:¬A(f,t).

passages.heading: 6-values-and-two-qualitative-judgments
passages.text: An embodied result requires a second judgment. For the accepted relationship and purpose ρ(t) and the requirement of mutual fulfilment μ(t), define

passages.heading: 6-values-and-two-qualitative-judgments
passages.text: EK,ρ(t),μ(t):Y⟶{agreement,unresolved,contradiction},

passages.heading: 6-values-and-two-qualitative-judgments
passages.text: Successful activity is represented as

passages.heading: 6-values-and-two-qualitative-judgments
passages.text: with M(t) denoting mutual fulfilment in embodied relationship. This guards against treating inward concurrence, correct intention, pleasure, or unilateral advantage as sufficient evidence.

passages.heading: 7-modes-and-effective-depth
passages.text: 7. Modes and effective depth

passages.heading: 7-modes-and-effective-depth
passages.text: Let Feff(t)⊆F contain the faculties effectively participating in the present activity. Delusion is directly described through four and a half effective activities: selection and taste in mun, analysis and deliberation restricted to pleasure, health, and profit in vritti, and visualisation in chitta (MVD, pp. 79, 89; JV, pp. 73–74; AVD, p. 152).

passages.heading: 7-modes-and-effective-depth
passages.text: The model represents this shallow depth without inserting effective bodh or anubhav:

passages.heading: 7-modes-and-effective-depth
passages.text: Feff(t)={c,v,m}.

passages.heading: 7-modes-and-effective-depth
passages.text: Partially awakened, half-awakened, and awakened statuses are represented by progressively deeper effective participation. Their source-given faculty relations are tabulated in the reader note §4.2; representing them as one formal transition sequence would go beyond the passages (MVD, pp. 278–279).

passages.heading: 7-modes-and-effective-depth
passages.text: The union of vritti and mun alone is associated with sleep or dream, where imagination is not evidenced in work and behaviour (MVD, p. 279). It supplies a directly stated shallow case of recurrent activity without present bodily execution; extending that possibility to a complete five-faculty recurrence is a model hypothesis.

passages.heading: 7-modes-and-effective-depth
passages.text: The fraction in “four and a half” concerns the restricted jurisdiction of tulan: pleasantness, health, and profit operate, while justice, dharma, and truth do not yet govern. Visualisation remains effective but necessarily carries excess, deficiency, or omission without enlightenment in truth (MVD, p. 286). The sources do not settle whether that flaw is part of the fraction or a second description of deluded chitran.

passages.heading: 8-pair-level-semantics
passages.text: 8. Pair-level semantics

passages.heading: 8-pair-level-semantics
passages.text: The sixty-one bal–shakti assignments are documentary facts of AVD, pp. 91–94, confirmed by the dyad order in MVD, pp. 328–348. A functional schema for a pair j belonging to faculty f may be written

passages.heading: 8-pair-level-semantics
passages.text: Pair⁡(f,j)=(Bf,j,Pf,j,Rf,j,Cf,j,Ef,j),

passages.heading: 8-pair-level-semantics
passages.text: where B is the established member, P its paired motion member, R the reality or relationship involved, C a governing criterion where stated, and E an evidential result where stated. The sources do not provide all five fields for every pair, so this is a research template rather than a recovered specification.

passages.heading: 8-pair-level-semantics
passages.text: No single relation connects all sixty-one pairs. The following families are analytical groupings rather than source headings:

passages.heading: 8-pair-level-semantics
passages.text: accepted states paired with readiness for projection, most clearly in buddhi;

passages.heading: 8-pair-level-semantics
passages.text: held conditions paired with outward evidence, including santosh–shree, svayatta–samriddhi, sukh–sfoorti, hita–svasthya, and tushti–pushti;

passages.heading: 8-pair-level-semantics
passages.text: relationships paired with an associated value, responsibility, inquiry, or form of progress;

passages.heading: 8-pair-level-semantics
passages.text: an act paired with its object, as in nireekshan–guna and ruchi–pehchan;

passages.heading: 8-pair-level-semantics
passages.text: sensory qualities paired with varied correlates such as bearing, nourishing, respiration, or affinity; and

passages.heading: 8-pair-level-semantics
passages.text: residual category pairs that do not establish a directional relation.

passages.heading: 8-pair-level-semantics
passages.text: The source columns rather than these families govern assignment. The unpaired glossary’s statement that medha bears kala is not imported into the paired definitions; that cross-list variant and the complete documentary evidence belong in the pair inventory §8.

passages.heading: 9-continuity-and-observability
passages.text: 9. Continuity and observability

passages.heading: 9-continuity-and-observability
passages.text: Index embodied lives by n and let tdeath end the current bodily association. Let ⊑ denote that established organisation is carried forward without specifying whether every aspect is preserved:

passages.heading: 9-continuity-and-observability
passages.text: S(J,n,tdeath−)⊑S(J,n+1,0),B(n+1)≢B(n).

passages.heading: 9-continuity-and-observability
passages.text: The sources state continuity of jeevan, later association with a body, continuation of attained understanding and satisfaction, and bodily association from about the fourth or fifth month of pregnancy (JV, pp. 20, 55, 77, 94). Acceptances toward completeness and knowledge, wisdom, and science moving toward resolution are said to be carried forward as prarabdh; prarabdh also names what remains between knowing, desiring, doing, and undergoing (MVD, pp. 90–91). Neither formulation gives a body-matching rule. The passages do not state this carriage relation, identify its coordinates, or establish equality.

passages.heading: 9-continuity-and-observability
passages.text: The interval without a gross body is not inactive: subtle activities are said to occur according to the indication of buddhi (KD, p. 31). The carriage relation spans that interval without specifying which subtle activities occur, how they alter established organisation, or how later bodily association follows.

passages.heading: 9-continuity-and-observability
passages.text: Later conduct may be represented as

passages.heading: 9-continuity-and-observability
passages.text: The inverse is non-unique. Similar conduct can arise from different combinations of carried organisation, present education, bodily condition, relationships, circumstances, and current selection. Conduct can evidence operative organisation but cannot by itself identify which part arose before the present body.

passages.heading: 9-continuity-and-observability
passages.text: This caution is strengthened by the unresolved sanskar variant. One passage calls delusion under animal consciousness kusanskar; another says wrongs are not accepted and therefore do not become sanskar (MVD, pp. 94, 315; JV, pp. 49–50). What is carried under either formulation is not yet settled.

passages.heading: 10-worked-example-a-family-resource-decision
passages.text: 10. Worked example: a family-resource decision

passages.heading: 10-worked-example-a-family-resource-decision
passages.text: The reader note §3.3 describes disagreement over the use of family resources. In the formal notation, χ(t) includes the relationship, competing needs, bodily conditions, available means, and the criterion of just fulfilment. The current organisation of the five faculties and that context may yield a bodily possibility:

passages.heading: 10-worked-example-a-family-resource-decision
passages.text: p(t)=Express(X(J,t),χ(t)).

passages.heading: 10-worked-example-a-family-resource-decision
passages.text: Its performance changes body and field through G, and H makes the resulting material use and relational response available as y(t+1). The qualitative judgment e(t+1) then asks whether the result agrees with the relationship, mutual fulfilment, and the Knowledge-reference. If contradiction occasions a question, Occ, Bear, Answer, and reception-constrained Uptake represent the possible inquiry pass; assimilation may update S(J,t).

passages.heading: 10-worked-example-a-family-resource-decision
passages.text: This instantiation does not imply that ordinary decisions traverse consciously reportable stages. It shows only how context, expression, consequence, evaluation, inquiry, and lasting change remain distinct in the model.

passages.heading: 11-diagnostic-distinctions
passages.text: 11. Diagnostic distinctions

passages.heading: 11-diagnostic-distinctions
passages.text: The model separates failures that would otherwise be grouped under “lack of knowledge.”

passages.heading: 11-diagnostic-distinctions
passages.text: Criterion inversion: a sensory or material criterion is treated as final, so repeated pursuit continues without stable satisfaction.

passages.heading: 11-diagnostic-distinctions
passages.text: Information without assimilation: terminology is remembered but does not govern valuation, deliberation, selection, or conduct.

passages.heading: 11-diagnostic-distinctions
passages.text: Repetition under an inadequate criterion: skill or habit grows without qualitative awakening.

passages.heading: 11-diagnostic-distinctions
passages.text: Meaning error: an attractive representation does not preserve the recognised relationship or purpose.

passages.heading: 11-diagnostic-distinctions
passages.text: Definiteness without resolve: a principle is verbally accepted but does not organise action.

passages.heading: 11-diagnostic-distinctions
passages.text: Resolve without competence: the understood aim is not fulfilled because planning, bodily capacity, skill, or means are inadequate.

passages.heading: 11-diagnostic-distinctions
passages.text: Unilateral evaluation: intention or personal advantage is taken as evidence without mutual satisfaction.

passages.heading: 11-diagnostic-distinctions
passages.text: Inquiry not raised: contradiction remains stable because no question is formed.

passages.heading: 11-diagnostic-distinctions
passages.text: Indication available but not received: the stated condition of receptivity is absent.

passages.heading: 11-diagnostic-distinctions
passages.text: Shallow uptake: a question or answer alters present thought without becoming stable orientation or conduct.

passages.heading: 11-diagnostic-distinctions
passages.text: Perturbation at a faculty: its own operation is treated as supreme when it is not in accord with the faculty inward of it.

passages.heading: 11-diagnostic-distinctions
passages.text: Downstream perturbation: unresolved causal or subtle activity appears in chitta, vritti, mun, prana, body, work, or behaviour without identifying one linear cause (MVD, pp. 215–217).

passages.heading: 11-diagnostic-distinctions
passages.text: Opaque bodily mediation: waves and named bodily stages do not yet explain why a specific sentient selection corresponds to a specific neural and bodily process.

passages.heading: 11-diagnostic-distinctions
passages.text: Over-attribution to an earlier life: present body, education, relationship, circumstance, and current choice are ignored.

passages.heading: 11-diagnostic-distinctions
passages.text: Embodiment reset assumed: later embodiment is treated as erasing established organisation even though continuity is the source claim.

passages.heading: 11-diagnostic-distinctions
passages.text: Unsourced schema treated as architecture: the reported twelvefold practical enumeration is used to constrain the model before its four sensory activities and source are located.

passages.heading: 11-diagnostic-distinctions
passages.text: These are analytical distinctions, not clinical categories or source-given diagnostic labels.

passages.heading: 12-limits-and-research-questions
passages.text: 12. Limits and research questions

passages.heading: 12-limits-and-research-questions
passages.text: State, motion, projection, and reflection. Can the activity-level partition and the source’s directional column headings be reconciled without declaring independent axes that no passage explicitly states?

passages.heading: 12-limits-and-research-questions
passages.text: Two grains of bal and shakti. How do faculty-level strength and orientation relate to the activity-level pair, especially where one passage recognises a faculty’s bal in both activities?

passages.heading: 12-limits-and-research-questions
passages.text: Uses of projection and reflection. How do directional movement, recognising and fulfilling, and understanding and making-understood relate?

passages.heading: 12-limits-and-research-questions
passages.text: Receptivity. Are the four absence-conditions binary, graded, or threshold descriptions of capacities that otherwise admit of degree?

passages.heading: 12-limits-and-research-questions
passages.text: Inquiry. What causes a standing thirst for understanding to become an actual question, and what source-grounded sequence replaces or constrains the proposed protocol?

passages.heading: 12-limits-and-research-questions
passages.text: Body relation. How do prana, heart, medhas, cognitive and work organs, bodily waves, and sentient content form a discriminating connection?

passages.heading: 12-limits-and-research-questions
passages.text: Mutual satisfaction. How can it be assessed without reducing it to agreement, compliance, or self-report?

passages.heading: 12-limits-and-research-questions
passages.text: Sanskar. Does acquired organisation exclude atma, and is a deluded organisation kusanskar or something that never became sanskar?

passages.heading: 12-limits-and-research-questions
passages.text: Continuity. What determines association with a particular developing body, which subtle activities occur without a gross body, how they affect established organisation, and what—if anything—is preserved without loss?

passages.heading: 12-limits-and-research-questions
passages.text: Behavioural evidence. What observations distinguish carried organisation from present learning and circumstance without circular inference?

passages.heading: 12-limits-and-research-questions
passages.text: Pair specification. Can the sixty-one pairs support a uniform functional schema when their stated relations and definitional fields differ?

passages.heading: 12-limits-and-research-questions
passages.text: Constitutional counts. Is the sequence 1+2+8+18+32 intentionally related to the shell-capacity expression 2n2, or is that numerical correspondence accidental?

passages.heading: 12-limits-and-research-questions
passages.text: Missing sound pair. Why do the closing sensory pairs cover touch, temperature, taste, smell, and visible form while sound appears only inside another definition?

passages.heading: 12-limits-and-research-questions
passages.text: Knowing, believing, recognising, and fulfilling. How does this source-grounded fourfold map, if at all, to the ten activities?

passages.heading: 12-limits-and-research-questions
passages.text: Sakshatkar. Does it name chintan under another aspect or the success of study at chitta?

passages.heading: 12-limits-and-research-questions
passages.text: The oral twelvefold. Where is the reported enumeration of four bodily propensities, four sensory activities, three eshanas, and upakar recorded? Until the four sensory activities and the complete set are sourced, it should not constrain the formal state.

passages.heading: 13-textual-variants-and-excluded-schemas
passages.text: 13. Textual variants and excluded schemas

passages.heading: 13-textual-variants-and-excluded-schemas
passages.text: 13.1 Uses of avartan, projection, and reflection

passages.heading: 13-textual-variants-and-excluded-schemas
passages.text: At MVD, p. 275, avartan kriya names the combined form of reflection and projection, the awakened jeevan cycle. At p. 291, the wording presents projection and reflection as the activities whose effects must be understood to avoid mysteriousness and decline. Insentient nature is also distinguished as having projection alone, while sentient nature has both projection and reflection (SB, p. 60). Projection and reflection elsewhere distinguish sensory recognition of form and properties from recognition of value, essential nature, dharma, and existence (SB, pp. 63–64), while another passage names understanding as reflection and making-understood as projection (KD §3.12, p. 110). The directional account formalised in §3 is therefore one source-supported use rather than an exclusive corpus-wide definition.

passages.heading: 13-textual-variants-and-excluded-schemas
passages.text: 13.2 Faculty locations and adjoining relations

passages.heading: 13-textual-variants-and-excluded-schemas
passages.text: Hope, thought, desire, resoluteness, and evidence are located at faculties in some passages and at the relations between body, mun, vritti, chitta, buddhi, and atma in another (MVD, pp. 275–276; AVD, p. 91). The model uses faculty coordinates for tractability. Awareness (pratiti), comprehension (aabhas), and perception (bhas) at three adjoining relations are retained in the reader account rather than introduced as extra coordinates (MVD, pp. 99–100).

passages.heading: 13-textual-variants-and-excluded-schemas
passages.text: 13.3 Sanskar, sakshatkar, and overlapping vocabulary

passages.heading: 13-textual-variants-and-excluded-schemas
passages.text: The four-faculty placement in §2.1 follows attained awakening in mun, vritti, chitta, and buddhi (MVD, p. 121). Delusion under animal consciousness is called kusanskar in one formulation, while another holds that wrongs are not accepted and therefore do not become sanskar (MVD, pp. 94, 315; JV, pp. 49–50). Sakshatkar appears where study reaches chitta and as realisation-based contemplation of enlightenment and resolve, overlapping the locus of chintan without establishing a separate faculty stage (MVD, pp. 99, 126).

passages.heading: 13-textual-variants-and-excluded-schemas
passages.text: Medhas names neural mediation, while medha is an activity of chitta associated with bearing memory and art (MVD, pp. 200, 330). Samvedna names sensitivity in one account and a detailed activity of vritti in another (MVD, pp. 273, 337). Sensing, enquiring, protecting, enlightening, adhering, and reflecting are also listed as sentient specialties; several concern inquiry, teaching, mutual resolution, protection, and human relationship rather than internal traffic among faculties (MVD, pp. 313–314).

passages.heading: 13-textual-variants-and-excluded-schemas
passages.text: 13.4 Documentary and oral exclusions

passages.heading: 13-textual-variants-and-excluded-schemas
passages.text: The flat glossary at MVD, pp. 323–326, and the paired definitions at pp. 328–348 are not identical. Their variants, the eight dimensions of visualisation, and the missing sound pair are documented in the pair inventory §8 rather than merged into the formal state. The reported twelvefold practical schema—four bodily propensities, four sensory activities, three eshanas, and upakar—remains excluded because no located source enumerates the twelve or names the four sensory activities.
